run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T01:08:46Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend-proxy error-rate deviation in this window is explained by a brief outage of its downstream cart service during a rollout. Deployment cart in otel-demo carries pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T01:11:16Z; the old pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 was killed at 01:11:19Z and the replacement pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz only logged 'Successfully connected to Redis' at 01:11:32.610912Z and started binding its HTTP ports at 01:11:41.911185Z. The cart container has no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe, so the pod was reported Ready as soon as its container started while the old pod had already been scaled down. frontend-proxy access logs show HTTP 500 responses flagged 'via_upstream' (generated by the frontend upstream) for GET/POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout from at or before 01:11:20.710940Z through about 01:11:48.9Z, and four 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} responses on /api/products between 01:12:33Z and 01:13:39Z. Consistently, frontend spans carry ERROR status on grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart (24.21), CartService/AddItem (54.74), CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (18.95) and tcp.connect (7.37), while cart's own error series in the same period are 0, so the failing calls were transport-level against cart rather than cart application errors. frontend-proxy ingress error spans rose by 93 in one 15s interval ending 01:12:30Z, the only large deviation of that counter in the observed hour. Unresolved: the annotation value 0.0111 and the RequestErrorRate rule could not be verified, and the alert's reported start 01:08:46Z precedes the first observed 5xx by about 2.5 minutes. Separate finding not tied to this cause: fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh restarted at 01:16:46Z with last termination reason OOMKilled (exit 137).

claims.text: Deployment cart in namespace otel-demo carries pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T01:11:16Z, has replicas=1 and RollingUpdate maxUnavailable 25%.

Kubernetes events in otel-demo show Deployment cart scaling new ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d from 0 to 1 at 01:11:16Z, that ReplicaSet creating pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz at 01:11:16Z, pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 being killed at 01:11:19Z, and ReplicaSet cart-755465879b scaled 1 to 0 with SuccessfulDelete.
The cart container spec has readinessProbe=null, livenessProbe=null and startupProbe=null (single container named cart, port 8080, limits cpu 45m / memory 165Mi).
ReplicaSets cart-755465879b (created 2026-11-17T00:40:06Z, replicas 0) and cart-84889c965d (created 2026-11-17T01:11:16Z, replicas 1, ready 1) are both owned by Deployment cart.

Pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz was created at 01:11:16Z, is owned by ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d, has restartCount 0 and is Ready; its cart container logged 'Successfully connected to Redis' at 01:11:32.610912Z and 'Overriding HTTP_PORTS ... Binding to values defined by URLS' at 01:11:41.911185Z.

frontend-proxy access logs show HTTP 500 responses with protocol 'via_upstream' for POST /api/cart, GET /api/cart and POST /api/checkout starting at 01:11:20.710940Z (newest 30 of 33 matching 5xx lines in 01:10:00-01:11:29Z, 3 earlier matching lines not shown) and continuing to about 01:11:48.9Z; a 01:11:00-01:15:00Z query matched 97 5xx lines.

frontend-proxy also returned 503 with response flag 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' for GET /api/products/{productId} requests at 01:12:33.717656Z, 01:12:33.962374Z, 01:12:34.006609Z and 01:13:39.557969Z.

frontend-proxy's ingress error-span counter rose from 596 (01:12:15Z) to 689 (01:12:30Z), i.e. +93 error spans in one 15s interval, while ingress spans rose from 20424 to 21071 in the same interval; the counter was 594 at 01:08:00Z and 695 at 01:20:00Z.

Across the observed hour the 5-minute increase of frontend-proxy error spans was 5.555 at 00:54:59Z, 4.444 at 00:59:59Z, 0 at 01:04:59Z, 1.111 at 01:09:59Z, 211.111 at 01:14:59Z, 2.222 at 01:19:59Z and 3.974 at 01:24:59Z; the 211.111 window is the only large deviation.

In the 10 minutes ending 01:17:00Z the error spans were attributed to frontend (grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 54.74, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 24.21, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 18.95, tcp.connect 7.37, executing api route (pages) /api/cart 78.95, GET /api/cart 24.21, POST /api/cart 54.74, POST /api/checkout 18.95) and to frontend-proxy (router frontend egress 97.89, ingress 105.26); cart's error series in the same period were 0 apart from flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream at 0.

checkout's own spans over 01:03:00-01:18:00Z show STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase 0 for both oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, with the same operations present carrying STATUS_CODE_UNSET values.
Pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh has restartCount 1 with lastState terminated reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-17T01:16:46Z, and a container Started event at 01:16:47Z.

At query time all 21 pods in otel-demo were Running and ready, with frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-v4lvt at restartCount 0; the cart endpoint is 100.96.1.157:8080 and the valkey-cart endpoint is 100.96.3.198:6379.

cart's Redis dependency was reachable during the restart window: the new cart container logged 'Successfully connected to Redis' at 01:11:32.610912Z and Service valkey-cart has endpoint 100.96.3.198:6379, so a valkey-cart outage is not supported as the reason cart stopped serving.

frontend-proxy itself did not fail: its pod was Running/ready with restartCount 0, and the 500 responses carry 'via_upstream' with a 21-byte upstream body, showing the 5xx were produced by the frontend upstream rather than by the proxy rejecting requests.

The fraud-detection OOMKill (exit 137 at 01:16:46Z) is not the cause of this frontend-proxy error-rate alert: it happened after the 500 burst on /api/cart and /api/checkout (01:11:20-01:11:48Z) and checkout's own PlaceOrder spans show 0 error status over 01:03-01:18Z.

The four 503 UC 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' responses on GET /api/products between 01:12:33Z and 01:13:39Z are a second, smaller error mode shortly after the cart rollout that is not explained by the cart restart itself and needs separate confirmation.

The missing readiness/startup probe on the cart container is what turned a routine one-replica restart into request failures: the new pod was reported Ready when its container started at 01:11:18Z although the app only began binding its HTTP ports at 01:11:41Z, while the old pod was already removed at 01:11:19Z.

Add a readinessProbe (and a startupProbe) on port 8080 to the cart container and, for a single-replica Deployment, use maxUnavailable 0 so a rollout does not remove the serving pod before the replacement actually answers.
Trace who or what issued the cart restart at 2026-11-17T01:11:16Z (rollout history / change records) and review the fraud-detection container memory limit given its OOMKill at 01:16:46Z.

gaps: The alerting rule RequestErrorRate was not returned by list_prometheus_rules (rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned nothing), so the expression and window behind the annotation value 0.01111111111111111 could not be verified; the nearest observable error-rate signal is the +93 error-span jump on frontend-proxy ingress ending 01:12:30Z.

The alert's reported start 2026-11-17T01:08:46Z precedes the first observed 5xx (at or before 01:11:20.710940Z) by roughly 2.5 minutes; the 5-minute frontend-proxy error increase at 01:09:59Z was only 1.111, so why the alert fired at 01:08:46Z is unresolved.

Jaeger queries returned no traces for frontend, frontend-proxy or error=true in 01:10:00-01:29:59Z (views with status no_data), so span-level error messages, status codes and parent-child call edges for the failing requests are unknown.
Metrics http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count returned no series in the window (no_data), so their status-code breakdown is unknown, not zero.

A log query on pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-64mj8 for 01:05:00-01:20:00Z returned no lines (no_data), so the frontend application's own error text for the 500 responses could not be read; a filtered query on checkout-5dccdccdd8-like pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-cph2g for 01:10:00-01:13:00Z also returned nothing and is not used as evidence.

The previous cart pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 and its template are gone, so whether the 01:11:16Z rollout also changed the cart image or added the wait-for-valkey-cart init container (versus only the restartedAt annotation) cannot be verified.
No change-history integration is available in this Run, so the actor and reason for the cart rollout restart at 01:11:16Z are unknown.
State of the series after 01:26:46Z (last frontend-proxy/frontend sample) and the current alert status are outside the delivered evidence and unknown.
next_steps: Add a readinessProbe and startupProbe to the cart container and set maxUnavailable: 0 for the single-replica cart Deployment, then re-test a rollout to confirm no 5xx at frontend-proxy.
Consult cluster change/audit history (not integrated here) to identify who ran the cart rollout restart at 2026-11-17T01:11:16Z and whether it was intended.

Locate the RequestErrorRate alerting rule in the Alertmanager/Prometheus configuration that produced the alert payload, since it is absent from the queried Prometheus rules, and confirm its ratio and window against traces_span_metrics_calls_total.
Investigate the fraud-detection OOMKill (container memory limit versus usage) as a separate reliability issue, since it is unrelated to this frontend-proxy error-rate alert.
